correctness.rationale: For p odd, p∤a, b>a, p|(b−a), d=a+b is a unit and v=(aα+bβ)/d is recovered from the degree-(d−1) coefficient. The invertible change α=v+bw, β=v−aw gives F(T)=(U−bw)^a(U+aw)^b. In characteristic p, b−a=p^e c and b≡a yield (1−bz)^a(1+az)^b=(1−a²z²)^a(1+az^{p^e})^c. Exactly w² and w^h (h=p^e odd) are recovered by nonzero coefficients −a³ and ac; all other exponents lie in <2,h>. Hence each finite-roots chart is k[v,w²,w^h]=k[v,x,y]/(y²−x^h), reduced and irreducible. Normalization k[v,w] is same fraction field, proper finite/birational globally; all forms in locus fit some linear-coordinate finite-root chart. Numerical-semigroup gaps 1,3,...,h−2 imply defect (h−1)/2 and conductor w^{h−1}; characteristic-p Jacobian of y²−x^h gives (2y,−h x^{h−1},y²−x^h)=(y,x^h), transverse singular length h. Independently recalculated examples (p,a,b)=(5,2,27), h=25, delta=12, and (3,2,11), h=9, delta=4; finite tests support rather than prove unrestricted result.
